drivers.driver: Equity earnings yields remain uncompetitive relative to short-term risk-free rates and long bonds [D04].
Market valuations are elevated with a trailing P/E of approximately 28.45x [D04].
Berkshire's massive scale limits the pool of opportunities that can meaningfully move the needle [D03, D08].
We refuse to force purchases simply to reduce our headline cash balance when prices offer an inadequate margin of safety [D05].

final.memo:
Charlie and I have always believed that the size of our cash balance is a consequence of our inability to find wonderful businesses at sensible prices, not a forecast of the next market decline [D01, D07]. At current levels, the S&P 500 offers an earnings yield of approximately 3.51%, which compares poorly to the 4.37% available on ten-year Treasury bonds and the 4.61% available on short-term bills [D04]. When risk-free instruments provide a superior yield to the residual earnings of equities, the margin of safety is simply insufficient for our requirements [D04, D06].

We are not in the business of predicting the market, but we are in the business of waiting for the market to offer us a bargain [D06, D07]. As it stands, we remain disciplined, holding our liquidity in short-term instruments that preserve our capacity to act when better opportunities arise [D01, D08]. We continue to hold our existing wonderful businesses, but incremental capital will remain in T-bills until the price of productive assets adjusts to reflect a more favorable risk-adjusted return [D06, D08].
